- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or shows sharp declines, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for risk reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% per day post-spike.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical mean (last 10–15 days) by 1–3% per day.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–0.3+), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often misses it — increase forecast sensitivity to early sentiment drops.
